evidence.V1: Classic cut-gem outline (wide girdle, tapered crown, pointed pavilion) reads instantly in front, three-quarter and silhouette; top view octagon with table also reads as a gem; outline symmetric, A15 X/Y error 0.0, apex centred under the girdle.
evidence.V2: Big crown/pavilion masses and medium table + girdle band are clear, but there is no small tier (no star/kite facets, no sparkle detail), so hierarchy stops at two levels.
evidence.V3: Proportions are a correct but generic octagonal brilliant: tall boxy crown with a large flat table over a short pavilion; reads as a stock primitive gem rather than a pushed, exaggerated stylised shape.
evidence.V4: Facet edges are all razor-sharp with no chamfer; the girdle band acts as the only transition. Facets catch light well (fits a gem), but there is no consistent bevel treatment of the ~0.045 kit kind.
evidence.V5: Close-ups (crown and pavilion, studio and flat) show clean planar facets with no pinches, seams, z-fighting or stray faceting; gates A17/A18 report 0 self-intersections, 0 cap overlaps, 0 flipped faces.
evidence.V6: One hue in three values (light table, mid crown, near-black pavilion) with strong value contrast; colourways (crimson, royal) keep the same disciplined three-value scheme.
evidence.V7: 64 tris against a tiny-class target of 150 (ceiling 300); no wasted geometry.
evidence.V8: Uses the kit's single white LF_VertexColor material with one hue in up to 3 values, but has no chamfers at all where the kit uses ~0.045-stud bevels, so it reads slightly harder-edged than kit pieces like the badge.
evidence.V9: Studio line is correct for a pickup: CanCollide off, CanTouch on, Box collision, Anchored, MeshPart.Color white for vertex colours, SmoothPlastic, origin centre.

top_fixes: Add a small-detail tier: split the crown into star/kite facets or add a bezel/upper-girdle facet row so the gem has a third level of detail and more sparkle variation
Add a narrow ~0.045-stud chamfer on the girdle and table edges to match the kit's edge treatment while keeping facets crisp
Push the proportions: deepen the pavilion slightly and narrow the table so the shape reads more stylised and less like a stock octagonal primitive
Lift the pavilion's darkest value a touch so the lower half does not read as near-black in the front view
